search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; explicit alpha/error-budget choice versus finite-horizon resolution; structured fixed-latent paired-sign policy game; boundary-null risk

numerical_setup.policy_library: 169 Bellman design pairs: q_low .60-.84 step .02; q_high .58-.82 step .02; wealth grid 320, action grid 61. Values are numerical approximations, not external empirical evidence.

alpha_resolution_pareto.interpretation: Every tested alpha lies on the basic risk-resolution frontier: raising alpha monotonically increases both worst-good deadline resolution and boundary false-commit probability. The marginal resolution gain per added boundary-risk point falls as alpha grows; from .03 to .05 the tested gain is ~9.07 pp power for ~1.81 pp boundary risk, while .075 to .10 yields ~6.47 pp for ~2.34 pp risk. This makes alpha an explicit deployment tradeoff, not a hidden constant.

utility_knee_sensitivity.utility: worst_good_power - kappa * boundary_false_commit, only as a stylized scalarization of the Pareto table
utility_knee_sensitivity.interpretation: The preferred alpha moves sharply with the relative cost of a false commit; there is no data-independent universal optimum. Around kappa=5 the tested grid puts the knee near alpha=.03-.05, while much higher harm cost pushes toward .01.

kappa2_relative_regret_solutions.note: For each alpha, map-specific oracle powers are recomputed at the same alpha, then a library mixture minimizes max{good-map regret, 2*boundary false-commit}. Because the oracle itself changes with alpha, the minimax-regret objective values are not directly comparable across alpha; the policy profiles are reported only to show how alpha changes bet allocation.

alpha_vs_bet_separation_strengthened.result: The good-map maximin policy stayed at the same structured inverted design (.80,.60) throughout alpha=.01-.10 while its threshold changed. This is direct evidence in the tested problem that the safety knob (alpha/threshold) can be varied independently from the alternative-side maximin bet geometry. The regret-optimal geometry did change with alpha because that objective explicitly trades map-relative power against boundary risk.
alpha_vs_bet_separation_strengthened.scope_guard: This separation need not hold for every alternative set/horizon. It is evidence for making alpha explicit and re-optimizing, not for freezing all bet policies when alpha changes.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Before deploying an anytime-valid evaluator, compute a task-budget-specific Pareto curve over alpha/error threshold versus worst decision-relevant resolution and boundary-null false-commit probability. Select alpha from an explicit harm-versus-unresolved utility or policy constraint; do not inherit .05 by convention.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: At T=50 in the structured paired-sign problem, alpha .01/.02/.03/.05/.075/.10 produced worst-good resolution .167/.250/.319/.410/.493/.558 and boundary false-commit .0085/.0174/.0274/.0455/.0686/.0920. Preferred alpha on a simple utility scalarization moved from .10 to .01 as false-commit cost kappa rose from 1 to 10.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: The numerical frontier is specific to the tested maps, discordance rates, T=50 and finite policy grid; alpha choice must be recalibrated when these change.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.update: Strengthened: in the tested maximin-power problem the same (.80,.60) alternative-side design remained optimal across alpha=.01-.10, while alpha alone traced the safety-resolution frontier. Regret objectives can still change the preferred bet geometry, so the two design dimensions must remain explicit.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: 'alpha=.05 is a neutral default for a self-modification gate.' It corresponds to one point on a deployment-specific risk-resolution frontier; different harmful-commit costs selected very different alpha values in the tested scalarizations.

Rejected: 'lowering alpha always requires redesigning the alternative bet geometry.' The tested maximin policy retained the same structured design over alpha=.01-.10, although this is not guaranteed under other objectives.

Rejected: 'minimax-regret numbers can be compared across alpha without qualification.' The map-specific oracle baseline changes when alpha changes, so cross-alpha regret levels mix a changing reference with a changing safety threshold.

Narrowed: 'realized null crossing being below alpha means unused error budget should automatically be spent.' The marginal power/risk return diminishes and depends on harmful-commit utility; conservative realized size can be intentional.

frontier.action: Compare one-stage alpha tightening with a two-stage proposal+fresh-confirmation design that has a fixed global error budget. Optimize the split of alpha and fresh-task budget for harmful-commit versus unresolved utility under the same structured maps.
Repeat the alpha/Pareto calculation at T=100 and under shifted discordance rates to test whether the apparent alpha-versus-maximin-bet separation persists.
Add rare catastrophic harm metrics whose null boundary is not captured by average paired-sign q=.5; require simultaneous safety evidence rather than scalar average success only.
Resume filtration-provenance and reused-development PACE-path selection/multiplicity once confirmation-stage error allocation is characterized.

exact_next_action: Construct a two-stage design in which a development/proposal-stage e-process and an independent fresh-confirmation e-process share a fixed global false-commit budget. Compare Bonferroni/risk-split thresholds and conditional confirmation strategies against the one-stage alpha Pareto at matched total task budgets, reporting harmful false commit, useful resolution and unresolved rate separately.
